learning_outcomes.text: Students should be able to collect and interpret relevant data (usually within their area of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Ability to work, lead and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies including information and communication technologies.
Ability to understand and apply the principles of basic knowledge of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and its application to problem-solving in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels and fluid systems.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply the knowledge on: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.

Understanding and mastery of the basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism and their application to the resolution of problems typical of engineering.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and computer programs with application in engineering.

syllabus_topics: Characteristics in Thermal Engines and power plants
Use of characteristic operating curves in steady state for diagnostic and predictive purposes
Predictive models in systems involving work
Modeling of thermodynamic transformations and cycles
Analysis of thermodynamic cycles in zero-dimensional or quasi-dimensional models
Influence of harmful space on compressor power and size
UD. 3.- THERMAL MACHINES BASED ON TURBOMACHINES
Flow direction in the impeller of a turbomachine
Transformation of mechanical and fluid energy in the impeller
Derivation of Euler's equation for motor turbomachines
Derivation of Euler's equation for generator turbomachines
Degree of reaction of a turbomachine stage
Thermodynamic study of the impulse stage
Thermodynamic study of the reaction stage
Characteristic curves and regulation of turbomachines
Gas turbines for industrial uses. Simple and advanced cycles
Regenerative theoretical cycle with intercooling and afterburning
Practical work: Characteristic curves in Volumetric Thermal Machines
Practical work: Thermodynamic models (zone 0) of Volumetric Thermal Machines
Practical work: Thermodynamic models and characteristics in systems integrating Turbomachines

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Completion of works, cases or exercises

assessment_rules: The global qualification considers 70% from a content exam (including exercises and questions) and 30% from directed work evaluated through continuous assessment. Both blocks must be passed separately to perform the weighted sum. For the content exam, students must obtain 50% in each of the three exercises; failure in any leads to failing the exam and the course. For continuous assessment, 100% attendance to laboratory practices (5% of final grade) and collective tutorials (5% for attendance and participation, 5% for delivery of associated work) is mandatory. Failure to attend these sessions or deliver the corresponding work on time will result in automatic failure of this block.
